body.en: After leaving Cape Town the boat faced strong *gales* for weeks, and the family celebrated Christmas in the middle of the stormy ocean. At dawn on 2 January the waves were gigantic. The crew slowed the boat by dropping the storm jib and trailing a heavy mooring rope in a loop at the stern. They lashed everything down, went through their life-raft drill, and put on lifelines, oilskins and life jackets.

steps.en: The family leaves Plymouth in July 1976

Two crewmen join for the southern Indian Ocean

On 2 January the waves become gigantic

The boat rights itself and he pulls himself back
Water pours in and Mary cries that they are sinking

explanation.en: Careful preparation came first; it was the great wave that turned the voyage into a fight for life.

body.en: In the evening a tremendous wave struck. The narrator was flung overboard, his head crashing against the wheel, and he believed he was going to drown. Then Wavewalker righted herself and he grabbed the guard rail and pulled himself back. Water was pouring in, parts of the deck and the side of the boat were smashed, and Mary cried out that they were sinking.

problem.en: What precautions did the crew take on 2 January, and why?

steps.en: They dropped the storm jib and trailed a heavy mooring rope at the stern to slow the boat.
They lashed everything down so nothing would fly loose.
They practised the life-raft drill and wore lifelines and life jackets.

answer.en: Expecting a violent storm, they slowed the boat by dropping the storm jib and trailing a heavy rope at the stern, tied everything down, and went through their life-raft drill wearing lifelines and life jackets, so they would be ready to survive the worst.
